  % Question 17
  \item Let $S_{n}$ be the sum of the first $n$ terms of the geometric sequence
    $\{a_{n}\}$, given $2S_{n}=3a_{n+1}-3$.

    \end{subquestions}

  % Question 18
  \item A factory is upgrading its production line with intelligent transformation.
    After the upgrade, 150 products are randomly sampled from workshops A and B for
    inspection, with the following data:

    \begin{center}
      \begin{tabular}{lcccc}
        \toprule
                   & top-grade & qualified & defective & total \\
        workshop A & $26$      & $24$      & $0$       & $50$ \\
        workshop B & $70$      & $28$      & $2$       & $100$ \\
        total      & $96$      & $52$      & $2$       & $150$ \\
        \bottomrule
      \end{tabular}
    \end{center}

    \begin{subquestions}
      \item
      Fill in the following contingency table:

        \begin{center}
          \begin{tabular}{lcc}
            \toprule
                       & top-grade & non-top-grade \\
            workshop A &           &  \\
            workshop B &           &  \\
            \bottomrule
          \end{tabular}
        \end{center}

      Can we be 95\% confident that there is a difference in the top-grade rates between
        workshops A and B? Can we be 99\% confident that there is a difference in the
        top-grade rates between workshops A and B?
      \item
      It is known that before the upgrade, the top-grade rate of the factory's products
        was $p = 0.5$. Let $\overline{p}$ be the top-grade rate of the $n$ sampled
        products after the upgrade. If
        $\overline{p} > p + 1.65\sqrt{\frac{p(1 - p)}{n}}$, then the top-grade rate is
        considered to have increased. Based on the data from the 150 sampled products,
        can we conclude that the top-grade rate of the factory's products has increased
        after intelligent transformation? $(\sqrt{150} \approx 12.247)$
    \end{subquestions}

    \end{subquestions}

    \begin{subquestions}
